a.xlink:title: Disable hardware interrupts (CLI).
Acquire exclusive access to a channel (blocks if busy).
Release exclusive access and wake any waiting caller.
Halt the CPU indefinitely.
Copy pending scancodes without consuming (irq snapshot).
Pop one raw scancode from the ring buffer.
Block until one event is available, then dequeue it.
Enable or disable relative mode (cursor pinned to centre, raw deltas passed through)....
Set the screen geometry used to clamp the cursor.
Prepare a channel for IRQ-driven command completion.
Schedule the next ready process to run.
Yield the CPU for one ~10 ms timer tick, then yield to any other READY user proc.
Wait for ATA command completion.
Sleep for the duration described by req (struct timespec).
Write sectors to an ATA drive (DMA if available, else PIO).
Read sectors from an ATA drive (cache + DMA/PIO fallback).
Kernel main entry point.
Exit the current process with the given exit code.
Check for deliverable signals and set up a signal frame if needed.
Replace the calling process image with a new ELF at pathname.
Terminate the calling process with status.
read(2) on stdin honoring the process's termios (ICANON, VMIN/VTIME).
Block until at least one layout-translated byte is available.
Read from /dev/tty — delegates to the keyboard line discipline.
Whether a read(2) on fd 0 could return a byte right now.
Report read/write readiness for /dev/tty.
DMA read/write through bounce buffer with retries.
Read sectors using PIO.
Write sectors using PIO with cache flush.
Read up to count bytes from the pipe's read end.
Write up to count bytes to the pipe's write end.
If a timer tick requested preemption, run the process scheduler.
Fork / clone (no threads): duplicate the calling task.
Wait for a specific child process to exit.
Wait for child process(es) to change state.
Read up to count bytes from fd into buf.
Write count bytes from buf to fd.
Wait for events on an array of nfds_u file descriptors (poll).
Monitor up to nfds_u descriptors for I/O readiness (select).
